item.title: [6] The piezochiral effect
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: A. Cavalleri, P. G. Radaelli

Authors: Z. Zeng, M. Först, M. Fechner, X. Deng, A. Cavalleri, P. G. Radaelli

Score 6/10 C_MAYBE

Why: New functional property with potential for spintronics/quantum info applications.; tier capped to C: formal/generic theory watch

Tags: #spintronics #chirality

Abstract: The piezochiral effect, a new member of the family of strain-responsive functionalities alongside piezoelectricity and piezomagnetism, is introduced, enabling control of chirality through mechanical strain, with future applications in photonics, spintronics, biosensing and quantum information.

item.title: [6] Perpendicular switching of polarization in layered ferroelectrics
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Javier Junquera, Ramamoorthy Ramesh

Authors: Pushpendra Gupta, Sergio Puebla, Fernando Gómez-Ortiz, et al.

Score 6/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Ferroelectric switching study, relevant to broader quantum materials field.

Tags: #ferroelectric #layeredmaterials

Abstract: Perpendicular switching of the polarization state in the layered ferroelectric Bi4Ti3O12 is demonstrated by means of trilinear coupling, allowing manipulation of the in-plane polarization component with an out-of-plane electric field.

item.title: [6] Weight-four parity checks in a spin-shuttling architecture
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Eliška Greplová, Lieven M. K. Vandersypen

Authors: Brennan Undseth, Nicola Meggiato, Yi-Hsien Wu, et al.

Score 6/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Semiconductor spin qubit implementation, relevant to the broader quantum hardware field.

Tags: #spintronics #quantumcomputing

Abstract: A silicon spin-qubit device comprising a shuttling bus for transporting qubits is used to achieve parity checks up to weight four, highlighting the feasibility and benefits of incorporating shuttling into semiconductor quantum processors.
